title: Computer Lab Technical Assistant
description: Assist the MIS team in maintaining student computer laboratories, performing routine hardware/software troubleshooting, monitoring laboratory usage, and assisting students during hands-on classes.
responsibilities: Check PC hardware and peripheral operability before daily lab sessions.
Assist students and professors with network login, compiler installations, and software tools.
Maintain cleanliness and enforce lab safety regulations.
Log hardware faults and escalate critical network disruptions to senior network engineers.
qualifications: Currently enrolled 2nd to 4th year BSIS, BSCS, or BSDS student.
General Weighted Average (GWA) of 2.25 or better.
Basic knowledge in PC troubleshooting, Windows/Linux OS, and local networking.
Responsible, punctual, and equipped with strong interpersonal skills.

title: Student Records & Archival Assistant
description: Support the University Registrar in organizing student records, encoding registration documents, sorting physical course binders, and assisting visitors at the information desk.
responsibilities: Scan and index student transcript documents into the digital archive.
Assist in receiving and sorting incoming student clearance and graduation applications.
Organize student physical 201 filing cabinets.
Provide courteous frontline queue direction during peak enrollment periods.
qualifications: Open to all undergraduate programs in good standing.
Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Google Workspace.
High attention to detail and strong adherence to data privacy and confidentiality.
Must have at least 3 consecutive free hours during weekdays.

title: Digital Cataloging & Library Aid
description: Assist librarians with book circulation, Dewey Decimal sorting, barcode scanning, thesis collection archiving, and patron assistance in the quiet study hub.
responsibilities: Check in and check out library reference books using the barcode circulation scanner.
Shelve books according to cataloging standards and perform shelf-reading.
Assist students and faculty in navigating OPAC (Online Public Access Catalog).
Monitor study areas to ensure a conducive, quiet learning atmosphere.
qualifications: Bona fide student with at least 1 remaining academic year.
Diligent, polite, organized, and fond of reading and books.
Can commit to either morning (8:00 AM - 12:00 PM) or afternoon (1:00 PM - 5:00 PM) shifts.

title: Peer Tutor - Linear Algebra & Discrete Math
description: Provide scheduled one-on-one and small group peer tutoring for 1st and 2nd year students struggling with Linear Algebra, Discrete Mathematics, and Calculus.
responsibilities: Conduct structured 1-hour tutorial sessions according to student bookings.
Prepare sample problem worksheets and concept explanation summaries.
Maintain student attendance logs and report progress to the Department Chair.
Encourage active problem solving and confidence building.
qualifications: Currently enrolled in BSCS, BSIS, BSDS, or BSCE.
Must have earned a final grade of 1.50 or higher in Linear Algebra and Discrete Math.
Patient, articulate, and passionate about teaching math concepts.
Endorsement letter from an ISM faculty member is a plus.

title: Science & Computer Lab Assistant
description: Assist laboratory custodians in preparing glassware, non-hazardous reagent solutions, setting up microscope benches, and conducting equipment sanitation.
responsibilities: Distribute apparatus to students before experiments and inspect returns for breakage.
Wash and autoclave laboratory glassware following strict chemical hygiene procedures.
Maintain reagent inventory and log chemical consumption.
Ensure proper waste segregation and disposal compliance.
qualifications: Enrolled in Allied Science, Computer, or Engineering programs.
Passed Chemistry/Lab fundamentals with high marks.
Strict compliance with lab safety goggles, lab coat, and chemical handling guidelines.

title: Gymnasium & Sports Facility Aide
description: Manage gymnasium court schedules, handle equipment rentals for badminton/basketball/volleyball, and assist athletic staff during intramural events.
responsibilities: Inspect and issue athletic equipment to students during open gym sessions.
Assist in scoreboard operation and tournament coordination.
Ensure safety protocols and court hygiene are maintained.
qualifications: Enthusiastic about sports and physical activities.
Dependable, proactive, and good team player.
Available during afternoon shifts or weekend tournaments.
